title: Legibility is Not Interpretability: Comparing Judged and Actual Importance in Chain-Of-Thought Reasoning
why_read: A careful empirical study challenging the assumption that chain-of-thought text explanations reflect what actually drives a model's answer, with direct implications for interpretability and process-reward-model research.
analysis: The paper operationalizes 'importance' of a reasoning step via Monte Carlo rollout-estimated advantage and tests whether LLM judges (and fine-tuned critics) can correctly identify which steps mattered, finding that judged importance only partially tracks actual causal importance especially for correct answers. This is a meaningful contribution to the ongoing debate about CoT faithfulness and legibility versus true interpretability, cautioning against naive use of LLM judges for step-level supervision. Directly useful for researchers building process reward models or interpretability tooling on top of reasoning traces.
